entry.title: Inside an Agent Runtime: Three Quotes, One Email, and No Duplicate Send
entry.summary: Follow a quote comparison through approval and delivery to see how the execution loop, model interface, tools, sandbox, and scheduler fit together. Then kill the process before it persists the receipt. What does the next machine need to take over?

entry.title: Storing Agent Transcripts: From a Tool Call to Recovery on Another Machine
entry.summary: Where should a 2 MB order breakdown live: the database, object storage, or the next prompt? Follow an order as it is created and compare what the Claude Agent SDK, LangChain/LangGraph, and OpenAI Agents SDK actually read and write.

entry.title: One Agent Sandbox per User: How Many Machines Need to Stay On?
entry.summary: Starting with Lester’s personal workspaces and Google Agent Substrate’s multi-sandbox Pods, estimate the fleet for 300 people starting at staggered times or all at once. Then trace what happens to files, processes, and publication receipts when a sandbox changes hosts.

entry.title: Why Does an Agent Need a Sandbox? From Compute to Deliverables
entry.summary: The model proposes a sequence of steps. Where does the program actually run? Files, processes, dependencies, and state explain how a sandbox lets an agent carry more tasks through to completion.

entry.title: Read, Edit, Write, Bash: The Design of Agent Tools
entry.summary: If an agent has Bash, why does it also need Read, Edit, and Write? Exact matching, pagination, output budgets, and execution status show how a tool can shape an agent’s next decision.

entry.title: How Agents Stay on Track During Long Tasks: Context Management in Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode
entry.summary: Using official documentation and pinned source snapshots, distinguish history, context, and memory. Then sketch a context layer with replay, explicit budgets, and verifiable behavior.

entry.title: Investigating a Cryptominer Disguised as sshd
entry.summary: High CPU usage led from a suspicious process to its executable, scheduled jobs, and configuration file.

entry.title: How an Invisible Character Shifted the Columns in a Data Export
entry.summary: A manual binary search narrowed the failure to a single row. Following the parser’s state transitions explained how a NUL character shifted the columns.

entry.title: Resolving Dependency Conflicts by Moving Spark into a Separate Service
entry.summary: Spark and the application’s existing libraries needed incompatible dependencies. Moving SQL execution into a separate service gave the caller a clear interface.
